name: Call the Coppercoats
oracle_text:
Strive — This spell costs {1}{W} more to cast for each target beyond the first.
Choose any number of target opponents. Create X 1/1 white Human Soldier creature tokens, where X is the number of creatures those opponents control.
blocked_sentences: Strive — This spell costs {1}{W} more to cast for each target beyond the first
Choose any number of target opponents. Create X 1/1 white Human Soldier creature tokens, where X is the number of creatures those opponents control

needs.what: a card-level additional cost that RAISES the spell's cost by a fixed mana string ({1}{W} here) once for each target chosen beyond the first, paid as part of casting, so the price is a function of the number of targets bound by a variable-size target spec
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Every price in card_level_cost_keys either lowers the cost or is a flat/optional extra: cost_reduction only subtracts and its cost_reduction_keys (count, total_power, greatest_mana_value, amount) each read the battlefield through cost_reduction_filter_keys, never the spell's own targets, and it cannot add. multikicker is the only per-instance repeatable price but it is optional and player-chosen, unlinked to how many targets were declared, so it cannot make the extra {1}{W} mandatory per extra target. Nothing in the pool prints 'more to cast' at all

needs.what: a way for an effect's value/selector to mean 'controlled by the players this spell targeted' — i.e. a controller/player reference resolving to the bound target players — so X can be count({types: [Creature], controlled by target players}) after 'choose any number of target opponents'
needs.why_existing_wont_do: controller and player accept only fixed roles in practice (you, opponent, any, each_opponent, each_player, owner, enchanted_player, gift_recipient); none of them narrows to the subset of opponents actually targeted, and with count: "any" targets that subset is variable, so counting creatures under 'controller: opponent' would count every opponent's creatures rather than only the chosen ones
